mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby driving negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25%, or the 20-day IC is >0.05 in a high inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite PAYEMS up and UNRATE down, or the interaction rank IC <0.02 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level indicates a turning point in supply constraints, prompting excess demand and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls then rises above previous month in the next two months
failure_condition: No significant return to trend in INDPRO, or 20-day returns remain negative when INDPRO shows a clear bottom.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months suggests the Fed will stay aggressive, raising rates and compressing equity valuations, which drives negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% month-over-month for two months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive when CPIAUCSL accelerates >0.5% MoM, or IC >0.1 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it indicates a shift to a restrictive policy, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in a non-recessionary regime.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive at the crossing, or 3-month IC remains >0.05 after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in job openings (PAYEMS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates labor market tightness that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, yielding positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE falls by >0.2% in the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative despite strong labor indicators, or interaction rank IC <0.04 over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in retail sales (not in the observable list, so skip demand proxy) — instead, use HOUST (housing starts) as a proxy: A 20% drop in new housing starts followed by a sustained rebound is interpreted as a bottoming cycle in construction, which supports optimism and drives positive 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >20% then rebounds above prior month in the next two months
failure_condition: No meaningful rebound in HOUST, or 20-day returns remain negative when the indicator shows a clear bottom.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as signaled by FEDFUNDS), the interaction between declining industrial production (INDPRO) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) creates a contrarian opportunity: S&P 500 20-day forward returns turn positive when both conditions coexist.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.2% while INDPRO falls and UNRATE rises over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite both INDPRO decline and UNRATE rise in a tightening regime, or interaction rank IC >0.1.
